description: Hands press, fold, and turn one soft mass again and again. 'pumeli' is this working of dough, clay, or similar material until its body changes. 'welotu' (mix) distributes separate materials; 'lupaki' (fold) and 'pesa' (push) name motions that kneading repeats and joins.
articulatory_notes: Close both lips for unvoiced 'p' and release into high-back rounded 'u'. Bring the lips together again for voiced nasal 'm', carry the voice through the nose, and open into stressed true-mid front 'e'. Touch the tongue tip to the alveolar ridge for lateral 'l', let the voice pass along its sides, and finish on high-front unrounded 'i'.
sound_symbolism: The lips close twice before the final lateral opens. That press, release, press, and release gives 'pumeli' a small bodily resemblance to the repeated work it names.
usage_notes: The dough, clay, or other soft mass is the direct object. A 'tei' (UNTIL) phrase can name the consistency or flexibility reached, and the event noun names kneading.

pillars.pre-industrial-wisdom: Dough and clay answer pressure, moisture, warmth, and time differently on each working day. Kneading places judgement in the hands that meet the material.

semantic_domains.activity: repeatedly pressing, folding, and turning a soft mass
semantic_domains.creation: working dough, clay, or similar material towards a usable condition
semantic_domains.physical: changing a soft mass through repeated pressure and folding
